newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania postpones again leu rate computing method.
newsitem.headline: Romania postpones again leu rate computing method.

text.p: Romania's central bank has postponed for the second week in a row announcing a new method of computing the reference exchange rate for the leu currency, which has been fluctuating since liberalisation last month.

"The National Bank (BNR) has agreed on the method, but the details will be available next week," BNR spokesman Adrian Vasilescu told a news conference, without elaborating on the reasons for the delayed announcement.
Three weeks ago, the BNR said it gave up computing the leu's reference rate after restoring local dealer licences to 24 banks, which are now market makers along with four others.
Banks' quotes on screens have been showing wide ranges over the past weeks, in contrast with the uniform previous policy, when the market had been curbed to only four dealers.
The reference rate has frozen at its latest value of 7,744 lei to the dollar, computed on February 19. Vasilescu said the 7,744 level was valid until a new method was announced.

The reference rate, computed since August 1994 when the BNR introduced a free-floating foreign exchange market, was a weighted average based on daily reports of market operators. It was a guidance rate used for statistical accounting purposes.
"Unfortunately, that rate was often perceived as a rate established by the BNR," said Vasilescu.
Vasilescu said the BNR would compute the new average rate, probably at noon, to help "a correct reading of the diversity of exchange rates on the market".
He insisted that the new rate would have only statistical purposes and would "help the economy and the population to know the daily picture of the foreign exchange market".
On Friday, dealers' quotes ranged from 6,000/900 to 7,410/8,400 against the dollar.
